title: How to spot a fake natty: downplaying the effectiveness of PEDs
summary: Argues that people who say steroids 'just help you recover and work harder' are often lying fake natties coping with their own use. PEDs are an X factor no amount of natural work can match; their potency explains why people pay for them and risk jail or bans, and enhanced lifters shrink without them while naturals can maintain or grow.

claims.claim: Anyone serious about lifting has researched PEDs; he has never taken any but has extensive knowledge of them.
A red flag of a fake natty is downplaying PEDs: claiming steroids don't make you big or strong and only let you work harder and recover faster.
Naturals can't look like enhanced bodybuilders regardless of hours: you could match their intensity, tonnage and frequency and still not get their results, since some pros aren't even that strong.
PEDs are an X factor whose effect can't be gauged, making pro bodybuilding a separate sport from natural bodybuilding.
Honest enhanced lifters admit how much PEDs help; those who built careers saying they don't matter are suspect.
If PEDs didn't do much, people wouldn't pay top dollar for pharmaceutical-grade products, risk jail where they're illegal, or millionaire athletes risk drug test bans.
Users who downplay PEDs are coping, trying to convince themselves they'd be great without them.
He appreciates some openly enhanced YouTubers, but put them in a room with only water, weights and food for two months and they'd lose lots of mass; a natural might come out bigger.
Enhanced lifters need the drugs not just to grow but to maintain, because their own hormones no longer work.
Studies show that taking PEDs while sitting on your butt builds muscle, so anyone saying they're not effective is lying.
